parallel.requirements: Recognized the need for a full jusText-compatible package: HTML decoding, DOM cleanup, paragraph making, heuristic classification, stoplists, packaging, exports, tests, docs/demo assets, and setup verification.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation ownership and delegated two research tasks: one child inspected upstream API/classifier behavior and one inspected stoplist packaging. The parent owned integration, final edits, tests, and delivery.
parallel.implementation: The parent copied upstream jusText sources, added or fixed lxml_html_clean import handling, mutable stoplist normalization, packaged resource loading, public API exports, packaging metadata, tests, and an integration fixture.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Child findings were returned into the parent trajectory, the parent applied patches to the shared project tree, included 100 stoplists and support files, and delivered a final project summary.
parallel.verification: The parent ran the original test suite, focused public API and integration tests, full pytest, setup.py verify, and attempted the requested submit command before official evaluation passed 61 of 61.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unresolved implementation or coordination defect remained in the official outcome; the only reported limitation was that the in-agent submit command was unavailable, while the harness later ran the official evaluation successfully.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same full package obligations, including source files, setup metadata, 100 stoplists, public API exports, compatibility fixes, docs/demo assets, tests, installability, and CLI smoke checks.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single agent retained all ownership: upstream inspection, extraction, patching, test fixture creation, packaging, local verification, and final response happened in one serial control flow.
serial.implementation: The serial run extracted the upstream source distribution, patched imports and API fields, added package support files including pyproject and docs/demo scaffolding, fixed pytest pathing, and strengthened the integration fixture.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial run integrated all work directly in the local project tree, performed editable install, verified stoplists through the CLI, updated README metadata, and delivered a final project summary.
serial.verification: The serial agent ran pytest repeatedly, fixed failures, ran editable install without dependency resolution, ran python -m justext --list-stoplists, and reran pytest before the official 61 of 61 pass.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unresolved implementation issue remained in the official outcome; the serial final response only noted that the in-agent submit tool was not available.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the prompt as a complete jusText package build with encoding, DOM cleaning, paragraph heuristics, stoplists, packaging, exports, and tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same prompt requirements and built a complete jusText-compatible package with the requested support files and tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement coverage difference is evidenced; both addressed the same functional and packaging obligations and passed official evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into parent-owned implementation plus two child research tracks for upstream API and stoplist packaging.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no delegation and kept inspection, implementation, integration, testing, and delivery in one agent.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used children only for research; implementation and integration ownership stayed with the parent, while serial performed the same sequence without handoffs.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received stoplist findings first and API findings later; the parent acknowledged and used the child reports while retaining final decision-making.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial gathered equivalent upstream and package context directly in one thread, so no inter-agent interface was needed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had handoff boundaries but no unresolved or conflicting interface contract; serial avoided handoffs by keeping context local.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel vendored upstream jusText, then patched core compatibility, stoplist loading, paragraph fields, exports, setup metadata, and tests after child findings and local failures.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial extracted the upstream package, patched lxml compatibility, API fields, setup metadata, README/support files, pyproject, and tests in one local flow.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both converged on upstream-based implementations; parallel added a public API test and root integration test while serial also added pyproject and demo/docs scaffolding, but both delivered a passing package.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Both child results reached the parent; the stoplist child returned first and the API child returned later, after which the parent explicitly used the API compatibility finding.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to join and advanced through local command results directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had result lifecycle boundaries but no missing return, unjoined implementation, or ignored child result; serial had no delegation lifecycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote the upstream checkout into /workspace while an API child was still active; that child noticed local import context but separated it from upstream/source behavior, and the parent still produced a coherent final tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial extracted and patched the workspace in a single actor, later fixing pytest pathing so local imports resolved consistently.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel exposed a shared-workspace context risk that the child recognized and corrected; serial had no concurrent reader/writer boundary. Neither had a final collision or contaminated deliverable.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran baseline pytest, focused integration/public API checks, full pytest, setup.py verify, and the official evaluation later passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran pytest after fixes, editable install, CLI stoplist smoke check, reran pytest, and official evaluation later passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both verified locally before closure and both passed official acceptance; parallel used setup.py verify while serial emphasized editable install and CLI smoke testing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used more wall time and tokens because it ran two child investigations, but completed in about 487 agent seconds and closed with tests passing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in about 314 agent seconds without delegation and closed with tests, install, and CLI checks passing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel was slower but not budget-constrained or incomplete; the extra coordination did not displace required implementation or verification.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current completed official evaluations passed 61 of 61 tests, so there is no discordant official outcome to explain. The parallel solution differed mainly by using two child research agents and then integrating their findings in the parent, while the serial solution performed equivalent upstream inspection, patching, packaging, and verification in one thread. The observable parallel coordination risks did not produce a retained adverse pattern because child results were returned and used, verification was repeated after edits, and the final artifact passed official evaluation.
parallel_contributors: Two child research agents supplied upstream API and stoplist/package findings that the parent incorporated.
The parent retained implementation and integration ownership and reran verification after patching.
serial_contributors: The single agent inspected upstream/source package behavior directly and handled implementation, packaging, and verification locally.
The serial run performed editable install and CLI stoplist smoke checks before final closure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used setup.py verify and added public API coverage; serial added pyproject/demo/docs scaffolding and README cleanup.
Parallel and serial both initially had borderline integration fixture failures and fixed the fixture before final verification.

candidates.reason: The parallel parent explicitly retained implementation ownership and applied the package patches itself; children were research inspectors, not omitted implementers.
The parent integrated child findings and all code changes into the final tree, so there was no unowned reconciliation of component implementations.
The final package, setup metadata, tests, and support files were assembled by the parent before closure and official evaluation succeeded.
The parent owned the end-to-end path from inspection through patching, local verification, final response, and official artifact submission.
Implementation was not blocked behind a mandatory serial preflight; the parent copied and edited the project while children were still running.
Investigation and implementation overlapped in the parallel run, and the later child result was used without leaving implementation incomplete or verification shortened.
No indispensable implementation, integration, or correction path was starved; parent implementation continued and reached passing verification.
Only two research children were spawned, the run ended far inside the cell budget, and no required work was displaced by fan-out.
Neither child was assigned implementation-scale work; both research children completed and returned usable findings.
The visible child tasks were scoped to upstream API and stoplists; their returned findings were usable, and no missing known requirement made child work unusable.
Children were not producing separately owned interoperating components; they returned research reports consumed by the parent, so no cross-agent component contract was missing.
No known finding is shown disappearing in transfer; both child handoffs arrived in the parent trajectory and were acted on.
The API handoff was long, but the parent reduced it into concrete compatibility patches; volume did not prevent consumption.
The child noticed local workspace context effects and distinguished them from upstream behavior, so no stale report was consumed as current truth.
The two child reports covered different research topics and no unresolved incompatible contract or report blocked integration.
The parent did not accept the whole task on file existence or child status alone; it reran local tests and setup verification before final response.
There was no replacement child or retry repeating prior work without checkpoint transfer; failures were local tests fixed in the same parent flow.

No separate agents wrote competing implementation paths; children investigated while the parent performed the actual source edits.

The parent copied and patched upstream sources, but no child-owned non-entry source was replaced or deleted.

The parent imported a source tree, but this did not replace another agent's final-tree work or invalidate child provenance.
